title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover ordering
author: Asha Patel
ci_status_details: All CI stages passed on merge: unit, integration, e2e-stability; one flaky integration test was rerun and stabilized.
description: Motivation: production incidents over the last two days showed the SLO enforcer could trigger ordered regional failovers under load due to insufficient backoff/hysteresis and an ordering race in the failover coordinator. This caused short-lived thrashing between regions and increased error budgeting for some customers. Summary: this hotfix adds conservative hysteresis to SLO enforcer backoff decisions, fixes an ordering race in regional failover coordination, improves observability for decision transitions, and introduces a feature flag for staged rollout. Changes are scoped and guarded by a feature flag; default behavior is safe for immediate deployment. The PR includes unit tests for the ordering fix, integration tests simulating high QPS and backend degradation, and an e2e stability test that reproduces the previous thrash scenario. Also added metrics and traces (slo_enforcer.backoff_state, slo_enforcer.failover_decision, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_latency) to make post-deploy debugging easier. Backport: this was cherry-picked to release/2026-02 as part of customer-facing hotfix process. Rollout plan: deploy to us-west-2 canary (5%) for 30m, monitor SLO and failover metrics, then promote to global if stable. If regressions observed, flip feature flag or roll back the release branch. Related: ENG-2147 tracked incident, ENG-2150 captures longer-term scheduler improvements.
